title: The town that turned
hookLine: only the people of Yunus turned back in time and were spared (10:98)

lines: A PROPHET, A WARNING, A MOCKING.
THE SAME ENDING, AGAIN AND AGAIN.
cards: Read the Qur'an's stories of earlier peoples in a row and a pattern shows up. A prophet comes. He warns.
The people mock him. The warning comes true. Nuh's people, 'Ad, Thamud, the people of Lut, Pharaoh.
Again and again, the same ending. So when yesterday's story ends with Pharaoh in the water, you might expect the next one to end the same way.
Then, a few verses later, Surah Yunus asks a question: why was there no town that believed in time? And it gives one exception, the town that gives the surah its name.

teach.b: Verse ninety-eight, in paraphrase: if only there had been a town that believed, and its belief had benefited it, except the people of Yunus.
When they believed, God lifted from them the punishment of disgrace in this life, and let them enjoy life for a while.
The Qur'an doesn't name the town; many commentators say Nineveh, on the Tigris, the same city named in the Bible's book of Jonah, which Jews and Christians read too.
The strange part: in the account many commentators give, Yunus wasn't there for it. Other surahs tell how he went off in anger, fled to a laden ship, and was swallowed by the great fish.

The commentators place the town's turning behind him: the people saw the first signs of the punishment, and they went out of the city together, men, women and children, and cried out to God, and turned.
And the punishment that was coming was lifted. So the surah that holds Pharaoh's too late also holds a whole city that was not.
The door that closes at the death rattle was still wide open for them, and they walked through it at the last moment, all at once.

The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ once said, in a hadith in Bukhari: don't say I'm better than Yunus son of Matta. The prophet who went off in anger is honored by name, and so is the town that turned behind his back.
One verse changes how you hear the stories around it.

how: Muslim preachers often tell the story of the people of Yunus when calling a community to repentance, as the Qur'an's example of a whole town that turned back in time and was spared.

o: the prophet sent to warn Pharaoh in Egypt
the prophet who built the ark on dry land
the prophet whose whole town turned back in time

games.q: the town that turned — tap the pairs.
p: the one town that believed in time
don't say I'm better than him

s: Yunus was in the town when it turned
in the commentators' account he had already left in anger, and the town turned behind him.
the Qur'an names the town Nineveh
it says only 'the people of Yunus'; many commentators identify it as Nineveh.
10:98 says the punishment was lifted from them
when they believed, the punishment of disgrace in this life was removed.

games.q: you live in a city. your prophet warned you, and left. now you see the first signs of what he warned about. what do you do?
o: wait and see if it's real.
go out together and turn back to God.
chase after the prophet and blame him.
games.why: commentators say they went out together, men, women and children, and turned. 10:98 says the punishment was lifted.

practice: Think of a pattern in your own life that keeps ending the same way: the same argument, the same late night, the same thing said too sharply.
Picture the moment just before it starts again, and picture turning, right there, in some small way. If you pray, you can ask God to turn toward you, the way He turned toward the town.

wordCard.voice: Yunus. The prophet whose people, after seeing the first signs of punishment, turned back and were spared, the one exception named in Surah Yunus. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: "the people of Yunus," the one exception named in 10:98.

carryVoice: Your line: it's not too late. A whole city turned in time. That's day four hundred thirty-one.
